messages.author: 6e4e10e46624db56
parts:
Dear Rue

I would like to ask about scale.model=T. 
In the old version of INLA I run this model

IGN1Model2<-Case~  f(IT0,model="rw1", constr=T,cyclic=T, scale.model=TRUE,hyper=igprior)+

  f(IT2,model="seasonal", constr=T,season.length=12, hyper=igprior3,initial=12)+  

  f(IT3,model="iid", constr=T, hyper=igprior3)+

  f(IS2,model="besag", graph=W, constr=T,scale.model=TRUE,hyper=igprior3, group=IT1, control.group=list(model="rw1",cyclic=T, hyper=igprior)) 


ptm <- proc.time()

IGN1ModelRun2 <- inla(IGN1Model2,family="nbinomial",data=DATA17,E=Expected, 

                         control.compute = control$compute,

                         control.predictor = control$predictor,

                         control.inla = list(tolerance=1e-20, h=1e-8,int.strategy = "eb", strategy = "simplified.laplace"))

proc.time() - ptm


The progrem is running well 



But when I used the new version inla I got message :


*** ERROR *** Group: cannot scale.model with option cylic=TRUE. Contact developers.


I don't understand why. Could you give me a solution


Thank you

Best regards

Mindra

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla]
parts:
it is not yet implemented. you can bypass this by setting the option to
FALSE, and you might adjust for this marginal variance:

> n = 10; diag(INLA:::inla.ginv(toeplitz(c(2,-1,rep(0,n-3),-1))))[1]
[1] 0.825


Here, the marginal variance is 0.825, close to 1.
